turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same p-i-n (inverted) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
My predicted top five are **c030, c038, c044, c097, and c088**. I prioritize candidates close to high-performing training configurations, using transport selectivity, interface chemistry, and processing compatibility to judge the changes. These are predictions: the data do not establish a uniquely certain ordering of the unmeasured devices.

| Rank | Candidate | Physics-based rationale and training evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | **c030** | Retains the **PTAA \| PMMA / PCBM-60 \| Bphen / Al** combination measured at **19.48%**, adding IDTT2FPDI on the electron-extraction side. PTAA provides selective hole extraction, while a sufficiently thin PMMA modification can reduce interfacial recombination. PCBM and Bphen provide electron extraction and separation from the reactive Al electrode. The added acceptor could improve interfacial extraction or coverage, although its actual benefit depends on energy alignment and thickness. This is the strongest high-efficiency reference configuration among the candidates. |
| **2** | **c038** | Closely matches **Au-np \| NiO-c / PCBM-60 / Ag**, measured at **20.0%**, with an added PEI electron-contact interlayer and a change from FTO to ITO. The Au-modified NiO hole contact is directly supported by that strong training result. Thin PEI can modify the cathode-side interface dipole and improve electron-contact selectivity. Its insulating character makes thickness important, so I would not assume an automatic gain over 20.0%. |
| **3** | **c044** | A well-supported **PTAA / PCBM-60 \| BCP / Cu** device. The closest training configuration adds C60 and reaches **18.85%**; another PTAA/C60/BCP/Cu device reaches **18.62%** with two-step spin deposition. PTAA suppresses minority-carrier leakage at the hole contact, PCBM extracts electrons, and BCP separates the fullerene from Cu. Removing the additional C60 layer introduces some coverage uncertainty, but the complete contact combination remains compelling. |
| **4** | **c097** | Almost exactly matches **ITCPTC-Th \| C60 \| BCP / P3CT-Na / Ag**, measured at **18.49%**, replacing the sulfur-containing acceptor with its selenium analogue. It preserves the selective P3CT-Na hole contact and fullerene/BCP electron-contact stack. Selenium substitution can change packing, polarizability, and electron affinity; I expect broadly similar performance, rather than assuming that substitution necessarily improves efficiency. |
| **5** | **c088** | Uses **PTAA / C60 \| BCP / Cu**, a combination reaching **19.085%** with slot-die deposition and **18.62%** with two-step spin deposition in training. Doctor-bladed PTAA/C60/BCP devices with Ag also reach **16.9%**, supporting compatibility with that coating method. Willow glass retains a glass/ITO optical-electrical platform, but coating uniformity and substrate handling introduce more uncertainty than for the conventional glass candidates above. |

The common advantage is **selective extraction at both interfaces with an intervening electron-contact buffer**, rather than simply a favorable metal work function. Those features can reduce nonradiative recombination and contact losses while preserving fill factor. I would not extrapolate the isolated **24.8% TmPyPB** result to unrelated electron-contact modifiers.

**Final: c030, c038, c044, c097, c088**
